title: Change the engine oil
summary: Drain the old oil, swap the crush washer and refill to the mark. The single most useful job you can do yourself.
tools: Socket or box wrench for the drain bolt
parts: Engine oil (grade and amount on your spec sheet)
Oil filter, if your bike has a cartridge filter

steps.text: Ride for about five minutes so the oil is warm and flows out easily, then switch the engine off.
Park on the center stand on level ground and set the drain pan under the drain bolt.
steps.caution: The engine and exhaust stay hot. Wear gloves and keep your arms clear of the muffler.

steps.text: Remove the oil filler cap first, then loosen and remove the drain bolt. Let the oil drain until it only drips.
Wipe the drain bolt, fit a new crush washer and thread it in by hand. Tighten it to the torque on your spec sheet.
steps.caution: Overtightening strips the threads in the crankcase. Use a torque wrench, not feel.

steps.text: Pour in the new oil with the funnel, about 0.1 L short of the full amount.
Refit the filler cap, start the engine and let it idle for a minute, then switch it off and wait two minutes.
With the bike upright, check the dipstick without screwing it in. Top up to the upper mark, not above it.
Check the drain bolt for leaks, then pour the old oil into a sealed bottle and take it to a shop or recycler.
